written.myAnswer: Computational Biology uses mathematical models, algorithms, and computer simulations to understand biological systems and relationships. It also involves analysing biological data, such as amino-acid sequences in proteins.

Biology links with Physics through Biophysics, which applies principles of physics to biological processes; with Chemistry through Biochemistry, which studies chemical substances and reactions in living organisms; with Statistics through Biostatistics, which analyses and interprets biological data; with Geography through Biogeography, which studies the geographical distribution of organisms; with Economics through Bio-economics, which considers the economic aspects of biological resources and projects; and with Computer Science through Computational Biology, which uses computational methods to study biological systems and data.
